text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
--Several hundred Danish jobs and export sales of about one billion crowns annually are at stake in a U.S.-Europe trade war brewing over import regulations for meat and poultry.
--The tax and finance ministries have agreed to cut the 6,000-strong Tax and Customs staff by 355.
--Public building projects worth 800 million crowns are being halted, to counterbalance a lack of qualified construction professionals and relieve upward wage pressure.

--The major banks are fighting a proposal for a 'people's bourse' where individuals can make very small transactions. The banks say that such a system, which already exists in Sweden, distorts pricing.
--Culture Minister Ebbe Lundgaard has proposed that the state privatise 49 percent of television channel TV2, retaining 51 percent.
--The number of long-term unemployed academics rose by 40 percent over the past year. Many have been jobless for over three years without receiving any offer of employement.
